attempts.outcome: A new strict-dispatcher all-record scanner read all five prepared official masters (1,178,548 records; raw artifact records exact subrecord denominator and file hashes) for little-endian references to DA13 0008998D, Da13Intro 000BEDEC, WEJS14 000BED92, and WEJS15 000BEDAF. The main DA13 plugin has 116 matching subrecords across 99 records. Besides the already-classified QUST/DIAL/INFO/SMQN/SCEN/branch/view references, the scan exposed ACTI 000E6C88 DA13EmptyVesselActivator and ACTI 000A1F1F DA13GooActivator VMAD references to main DA13, plus ACHR 00045F8E. Dawnguard.esm contributes only the expected Story Manager node-child refs; Update/HearthFires have zero hits; Dawnguard has three hits and Dragonborn one. This expands coverage beyond the prior QUST/DIAL/INFO screen. The two activator scripts and the ACHR VMAD are the next source discriminants; raw byte hits alone do not establish Start/SetStage semantics or runtime reachability.

ACTI 000E6C88 DA13EmptyVesselActivator binds DA13EmptyVesselScript and main DA13. Its extracted base-Misc-BSA PEX OnActivate checks for Deathbell, Vampire Dust, a flawless ruby, and a silver ingot; on success it removes those items, calls DA13.SetStage(21), disables/deletes the activator, and shows a clue. No explicit level or DA13-stage predicate appears in that successful branch. This is a concrete potential pre-gate startup writer, subject to activator placement/enable state and exact Steam SetStage behavior. ACTI 000A1F1F DA13GooActivator binds a PEX whose player activation only advances DA13 to stage 30 when current stage is 21, and stage 80 when current stage is in [75,100); its other branches stage-check or activate Peryite, so it is downstream. ACHR 00045F8E has DA13OrchendorSCRIPT; OnDeath requests stage 73 and is likewise not a startup writer. All three PEX files parsed fully from Skyrim - Misc.bsa with no trailing bytes. The PEX/property route is static and does not prove the activator is reachable/enabled or the call succeeds on Steam.

The placed Empty Vessel is REFR 000E6C89 based on ACTI 000E6C88; its header flags are 0x00000C00, which the pinned TES5Edit schema maps to Persistent (bit 10) plus Initially Disabled (bit 11), and it has no XESP subrecord. The only official-master references to REFR 000E6C89 found in the all-signature byte scan are this placement and DA13 QUST VMAD property  on alias script DA13KeshSCRIPT. That alias is Kesh (alias 0, fixed ACHR 0008998C); its extracted PEX has only an OnDeath call enabling the Empty Vessel. Kesh ACHR flags are 0x400 (Persistent, not Initially Disabled). Thus the direct SetStage(21) activator callback is statically behind an initially-disabled reference whose only identified writer is a script on the level-gated DA13 Kesh alias; it is not an independent pre-start route in the inspected official records. The level-12 SMQN, level-10 WEJS14 handoff, main-owned DIAL stage writers, and downstream Goo/Orchendor scripts remain the identified paths. This is a source-level dependency inference; loaded enable state, alias lifecycle, complete-profile winner, exact Steam SetStage result, and level-one access are unobserved.

The hash-verified Skyrim.esm group walk places Empty Vessel REFR 000E6C89 and DA13 Kesh ACHR 0008998C in the same exterior CELL 00000D74 under Tamriel WRLD 0000003C; both are in the cell persistent-children group. The Kesh base NPC_ 00089986 is DA13PeryiteMonk. The ACHR and NPC_ records have no VMAD; DA13KeshSCRIPT is attached only to main DA13 alias 0 Kesh in QUST 0008998D, with its emptyVessel property pointing to the initially disabled REFR. DA13PlayerSCRIPT is attached to the DA13 Player alias and only updates ingredient objectives after GetStageDone(DA13,10) and before stage 15; its bounded PEX body has no Start/SetStage call. This confirms the Empty Vessel trigger depends on the quest-owned Kesh alias callback, while the Kesh physical reference itself is persistent and present. Cell membership does not establish physical approach, loaded alias state, or level-one dialogue availability.

The bounded source pass supports Q46-H1 below level 12: WEJS14 has GetLevel >=10 and its Afflicted Refugee dialogue sets WEJS14 stage100, then Da13Intro stage1, the intro scene, helper stage100, and main DA13.Start. This falsifies the all-starts-at-12 model within official records and captured base-Misc PEX. The group-aware join covers 23 main DA13 topics plus the helper and 26 INFOs; main-owned TIFs request stages 1,5,10,15,20,21,31,40,45,81,100 with no main Start call. Unconditioned INFO 000A1A65 requests stage21, but stopped-owner availability remains unknown. Empty Vessel is Initially Disabled and its only identified enabler is the main quest Kesh alias; Goo, Orchendor, and WEJS15 are downstream. The generic Orchendor alias PEX was not found by the tested extractor; properties show preReqStage40 and StageToSet75, without verifying callback semantics. No level-one/runtime/profile winner or OBJ-2 causal edge is established.

The 128-entry bounded GOG TESQuest vtable read at RVA 0x17E7D10 maps zero-based slot 19 (entry RVA 0x17E7DA8) to raw target 0x1403C8420/FUN_1403c8420. This confirms a virtual dispatch identity within the existing GOG 1.6.1179.0 project; it does not assign a semantic method name or imply Steam RVA equivalence.

Read-only direct TES4 captures show QUST DNAM bytes DA02 000160000000000007000000, DA04 11013c000000000007000000, DA06 00013c000000000007000000, and Update.esm DA09 00013c000000000007000000. The versioned TES5Edit dev-4.1.6 QUST schema parses the first two DNAM bytes as flags and names bit 0 Start Game Enabled (EV-0301 and primary schema source). Thus DA04 has bit 0 set while DA02/06/09 do not. These exact source flags align with parser-loaded +0xDC flags, subject to confirming the parser read width/write path; source files are official prepared masters, direct parser only, not xEdit or active-profile winners.
attempts.new_discriminant: If the parser copies DNAM flags to +0xDC, DA04 must load bit 0 set while DA02/DA06/DA09 load it clear; if +0xDC bit 0 is purely independent runtime state, source differences need not match and another constructor or mutator must define the value.

attempts.outcome: The QUST parser decomp confirms the DNAM branch reads its record block and writes the first 16-bit value to TESQuest+0xDC, then writes adjacent bytes at +0xDE/+0xDF; the legacy DATA branch writes its first byte into the +0xDC word and its second byte at +0xDE. TES5Edit dev-4.1.6 identifies the first DNAM U16 as quest General.Flags and bit 0 as Start Game Enabled. The remaining scoped writer FUN_1403c7490 initializes +0xE0=-1 and ORs 0x0100 into +0xDC; it does not set bit 0. Separately, TESQuest vtable slot 19 targets FUN_1403c8420, whose body conditionally clears bit 0. Combined with the exact four records, the serialized DNAM flag seeds the inspected GOG +0xDC bit 0, and a later virtual operation can clear it; the evidence does not identify when that operation runs or establish Steam runtime behavior.
attempts.new_discriminant: At load time, DNAM bit0 predicts +0xDC bit0 exactly for these records; if a later virtual transition changes readiness independently, snapshotting before and after that exact dispatch should show a 1-to-0 transition without altering serialized DNAM.

attempts.outcome: EV-0316 note and 63-artifact capture manifest are registered. Claim CL-L150 and mechanism M-0050 now map QUST DNAM.General.Flags bit 0 through the GOG parser to TESQuest+0xDC.0 and the SetStage predicate; the knowledge graph records this OBJ-1 causal chain and preserves no OBJ-2 edge. EXP-0057 separates supported serialized initialization from the later slot-19 clear path whose timing remains unresolved. Q-0056 hypotheses now mark independent initialization falsified and the later clear operation supported; Q-0057 is added as a dependent static dispatch-timing investigation.
attempts.new_discriminant: A callsite/order trace for TESQuest slot 19 should decide whether the virtual clear executes after DNAM parse but before SetStage eligibility, or only after that first guard; otherwise the exact Steam before/after callback observer is required.

decision.summary: Closed Q-0056 as a bounded GOG/source initialization result. EV-0316 traces the QUST DNAM first U16 to TESQuest+0xDC, maps bit 0 to Start Game Enabled under the versioned TES5Edit schema, and compares DA02/DA04/DA06/DA09 source flags. This supports serialized initialization and falsifies independent initialization in the inspected GOG path. A separate TESQuest vtable-slot-19 routine can clear the bit later, but its timing and target-quest reachability remain unresolved. No Steam behavior, natural callback, running state, alias fill, functional access, or level-one transition is established.
decision.cross_domain_assessment: The result adds a causal chain within OBJ-1 from serialized QUST flags to a GOG runtime field consumed by the SetStage entry predicate. No shared native call, ActorValue, HitData field, ActiveEffect, armor-skill award, or serialization dependency links it to the OBJ-2 armor-hit/XP path; no cross-objective causal edge is justified. Keep the exact Steam level-one observer and OBJ-2 protection/raw-AVSK discriminator open.

items.question: Does GOG TESQuest vtable slot 19 (FUN_1403c8420) run after QUST parsing in file-load finalization, and what is its relative order to the first natural Quest.SetStage callback?

hypotheses.model: In GOG AE 1.6.1179.0, slot 19 is dispatched in the post-file-load FormType sweep after QUST parsing and registration; whether the pass precedes the first natural Quest.SetStage callback remains unknown.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: A TESQuest-compatible slot-19 call appears in the load-manager chain after QUST record parsing and FormType registration.

hypotheses.model: Slot 19 is invoked only by later quest lifecycle transitions; no load-time call follows QUST parsing.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: No TESQuest slot-19 call appears in the post-file-load type-array sweep; class-resolved calls belong only to later start/stop/reset transitions.

methods: Verify the existing GOG 1.6.1179.0 identity and inspect references to the vtable slot-19 entry and its function pointer in the existing project, read-only with auto-analysis disabled.
Search indirect call operands for the TESQuest slot offset, then classify candidate callers by vtable provenance and object type; displacement hits alone are not attribution.
Trace any TESQuest-specific caller chain against QUST parse/finalization and the registered SetStage callback; preserve unresolved indirect sites and avoid assigning an undocumented method name.

The first natural SetStage callback order remains unresolved; record the exact Steam read-only observer test for the field before/after natural callback delivery, with no stage, level, flag, or event-context forcing.
items.next_action: Complete TX-20261017-0004/Q-0057 as a bounded GOG static finding, record the OBJ-1 graph update and no OBJ-2 edge, then automatically select the next ready P0 item and continue.

attempts.outcome: The fresh address-context query confirms the vtable slot-19 cell at GOG RVA 0x17E7DA8 is data, has no analyzed function boundary, and reports zero references to the slot address; the surrounding bounded window has no instruction at the cell. This is a narrow indirect-dispatch limitation, not evidence that the method is never called. EV-0316 independently records the cell value as FUN_1403c8420.
attempts.new_discriminant: A secondary function-pointer or relative-offset table reference at RVA 0x36368CC may expose an initialization/dispatch registry even though the vtable cell has no direct code xrefs; inspect it before broad slot-offset matches.

attempts.outcome: Address-context inspection of the secondary data reference at RVA 0x36368CC reports zero xrefs and no instruction at the data address. The source xref captured in EV-0316 shows a 32-bit word equal to FUN_1403c8420 RVA in a sequence of nearby code-like values, but the table schema and use remain unknown; this is not yet a dispatch site.
attempts.new_discriminant: If the secondary table stores relative code pointers and is consumed by a dispatch routine, its neighboring entries and xrefs may identify a call selector; otherwise only vtable-offset sites can decide load versus later lifecycle timing.

attempts.outcome: The bounded 8-entry read at RVA 0x36368C4 shows the data containing FUN_1403c8420 is not an ordinary 64-bit pointer table: one row is raw 0x003C8904003C8420, two adjacent 32-bit code-like values, with both targets unresolved as a combined 64-bit word. No analyzed references to the table entry were returned. Its schema/consumer remain unknown and it does not establish call timing.
attempts.new_discriminant: Any slot-0x98 candidate must be narrowed to TESQuest by a vtable-base or receiver-flow connection; the same displacement occurs across unrelated classes and cannot alone distinguish load from lifecycle dispatch.

attempts.outcome: The identity-checked GOG displacement scan completed with every adapter completion marker true: 4,307 total +0x98 operand accesses and 996 writer-candidate functions, mostly unrelated data fields. Filtering the preserved raw scan for indirect CALL/JMP operands yielded 212 sites across the binary. Eleven fall in the 0x140300000–0x140400000 code range; none is in known FUN_1403c6ff0, QUST parser FUN_1403c7a50, slot-19 target FUN_1403c8420, EnsureQuestStarted FUN_1403c9d30, or SetStage FUN_14034de90. The 11-code-range list is still only a broad location filter, not class attribution.
attempts.new_discriminant: If any candidate callsite receiver is a TESQuest instance from the QUST load/start manager, it may resolve H1/H2; if receiver provenance points to unrelated classes, discard it and continue the bounded candidate set.

attempts.outcome: Fresh GOG decompilation of FUN_1403b16a0 and its sole direct caller FUN_1401bdf20 shows array iteration and slot-0x98 calls over several manager-owned lists during a broad cleanup/shutdown-like routine; the receiver objects are not class-resolved to TESQuest, and no call order relative to QUST load or SetStage is established. This remains a broad displacement candidate, not evidence that TESQuest slot 19 dispatches here.
attempts.new_discriminant: A TESQuest dispatch candidate must trace the indirect receiver to the TESQuest vtable or an object known to be a TESQuest and place the caller on a load/finalization path after QUST parsing; generic manager arrays without this receiver provenance cannot distinguish slot-19 dispatch.

attempts.outcome: Fresh GOG decompilation of FUN_1403e6e60 shows a guarded object fix-up path over children stored at param_1+0x48; it writes each child parent pointer at +0x20, then calls the child vtable slot +0x98. The caller count is zero, and the parent/child classes are not resolved to TESQuest. Four data references to the function are present, but no caller order relative to QUST parse or SetStage is shown.
attempts.new_discriminant: A candidate is relevant only if dataflow or a concrete class/vtable reference shows that the +0x98 receiver is a TESQuest and its execution is ordered after the QUST DNAM parser write; this object-child fix-up lacks both links so far.

attempts.outcome: Fresh GOG decompilation shows FUN_1403e6fb0 resolves object references against param_2 and then iterates param_1+0x48 children, setting each child parent pointer before invoking child vtable+0x98. Its two direct callers FUN_1403d2fd0 and FUN_1403d3450 collect and priority-sort manager-owned object lists before calling it; FUN_1403d3450 also tests param_1+0xDC bit 4. This is consistent with generic object/reference finalization, but neither candidate receiver class is resolved to TESQuest and the call order relative to the QUST parser and Quest.SetStage remains unknown.
attempts.new_discriminant: If any remaining receiver resolves to TESQuest or a typed quest collection and its caller is ordered after FUN_1403c7a50 but before FUN_14034de90 callback delivery, that supports H1; if the remaining callsites resolve only to other classes or later quest operations, H2 gains support. Displacement alone cannot decide.

attempts.outcome: Fresh GOG decompilation of FUN_140305e80 resolves serialized references at typed TESForm fields to TESClimate, BGSEncounterZone, TESWaterForm, TESWorldSpace, and other classes, then invokes vtable+0x98 on an object at param_1+0x88. No analyzed direct caller of FUN_140305e80 or TESQuest receiver provenance was returned; this typed field mix does not identify a QUST path.
attempts.new_discriminant: A +0x98 call is attributable to slot 19 only when its receiver vtable resolves to TESQuest or a known TESQuest object; typed environment-form references in this function are not that evidence.

Thirteen direct call edges from twelve caller functions were returned across several code regions; receiver type is not resolved to TESQuest and the decompiled paths do not establish a QUST load/finalization ordering.

attempts.outcome: Fresh GOG decompilation of FUN_14030cc70 is a one-argument wrapper that returns 1 and, when non-null, calls the supplied receiver vtable+0x98. Its only analyzed direct caller is FUN_140305e80, whose typed references include TESClimate, BGSEncounterZone, TESWaterForm, and TESWorldSpace records. This call is therefore part of that unresolved environment-form child processing path; no TESQuest receiver is shown.

attempts.outcome: Fresh GOG decompilation shows FUN_140311820 iterating an object pointer array at param_1+0x28, calling each non-null receiver vtable+0x98, then applying FUN_140310160 and compacting/removing entries. items.question: Can the official Resist Magic clothing candidate ARMO 000FC061 provide a level-one player with measurable protection from incoming magic attacks while the Heavy/Light skill route remains at zero, and is this a distinct damage path rather than a positive-DNAM HitData bypass?

hypotheses.model: The level-one-accessible clothing enchantment modifies AV44 and reduces resistable magic damage through MagicTarget::CheckResistance, while its zero physical DNAM rating leaves it outside the mapped positive-DNAM Heavy/Light selector.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: The exact vanilla item and acquisition path are confirmed; a controlled incoming magic hit causes positive but lower Health damage with the item, while repeated numeric Heavy/Light AVSK samples stay unchanged and no AV11/AV12 hit-award call is observed.

hypotheses.model: The clothing resistance path protects against magic effects only and does not demonstrate armor-like protection against the qualifying physical hit required for the bounty prize.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: Paired controls show reduced damage from an AV41-44-resistable magic effect but no reduction from a comparable physical hit; the magic path remains separate from the mapped HitData/AV11/AV12 branch.

methods: Verify the exact five-master ARMO/ENCH/MGEF chain and identify a natural level-one acquisition route for ARMO 000FC061; source records alone do not establish player access.
Trace the ordinary incoming magic-effect route into MagicTarget::CheckResistance and determine whether it enters any HitData or Heavy/Light skill-use path; keep GOG and Steam identities separate.

When the verified Steam test lane and disposable save/Observer prerequisites are available, compare naked and equipped controls under the same resistable magic attack, recording nonzero Health damage, numeric Heavy/Light/Block AVSK before and after repeated hits, level, item slot and all other effects.
Run a separate physical-hit control. If only magic damage is reduced, classify this as a defensive-apparel comparator or partial result, not proof of a general physical-armor XP bypass.
